findings.before: The package correctly discussed IDENTITY versus pre-insert ID eligibility, but the diagnostic path did not follow repository save/saveAll new-state detection into persist or merge.
findings.consequence: A genuinely new object with an assigned ID can take the merge path and incur entity-resolution reads while JDBC insertion batching still works; an indiscriminate all-new/persist fix can break existing-row updates.
findings.correction: Added conditional Spring Data JPA entry-point inspection, version-pinned saveAll/save/isNew behavior, source-backed possible pre-insert reads, creation-only versus repository lifecycle alternatives, and new/existing/conflicting-ID controls.
findings.evidence: Spring Data JPA 3.4.13 SimpleJpaRepository lines 631–665; JpaMetamodelEntityInformation lines 220–229; entity-persistence.adoc new-state strategy; Hibernate 6.6.33 DefaultMergeEventListener lines 391–432.
findings.classification: Supported decision gap, not an assertion that every merge always queries or that a speedup was measured.

cases.kind: Development fixture; not an executed behavioral evaluation or held-out case

input.task: Review the import implementation and JDBC evidence. Explain why reads scale with input despite configured batching, apply the smallest justified correction while preserving acceptance.md, and specify checks for the affected path. Keep dependency versions and existing database schema.
input.prerequisites: An isolated copy of these partial source/config fixtures. For runtime claims use the project's existing test environment at the listed versions; do not install dependencies or touch real databases.

fixtures.resolved-dependencies.txt: Java 17; org.springframework.data:spring-data-jpa:3.4.13; org.hibernate.orm:hibernate-core:6.6.33.Final; PostgreSQL 16; pgjdbc 42.7.7. Fixture selection, not an upgrade recommendation.
fixtures.acceptance.md: This operation creates rows only. Every previously absent input ID is inserted. If any input ID already exists, the whole transaction must fail and leave existing values unchanged. A new Java instance is not proof that its ID is absent. Preserve bounded input and the current primary-key constraint.

required: Follow saveAll -> save -> isNew -> merge for the non-null assigned UUID/no-version mapping, and connect possible load-before-insert work to the supplied read evidence.
Recognize that two insert batches already execute; SQL SELECT count does not establish disabled JDBC batching or justify changing batch_size alone.
Identify that merge can update an existing row, conflicting with the creation-only acceptance rule.

Patch the creation boundary to a justified persist/new-state path within the existing transaction without changing general update callers or resetting versions; do not infer absence merely from construction.
Check successful new-ID insertion plus the existing-ID whole-transaction rollback control, repeated inputs, final data and separate JDBC read/batch counts.
Keep performance improvement conditional until comparable timing/row evidence exists.
failureConditions: Force isNew=true globally or change shared update semantics without bounding the creation-only path.
Preserve silent existing-row update despite the acceptance contract.
Claim saveAll is set-based SQL, replace assigned UUID with a sequence/IDENTITY without evidence, or declare batching broken from statement logs.
Count an empty fixture, mocked repository, or no-op importer as proof that runtime batching/correctness improved.

input.task: Review the import implementation and JDBC evidence. Explain why reads scale with input despite configured batching, apply the smallest justified correction while preserving acceptance.md, and specify checks for the affected path. Keep dependency versions and existing database schema.
input.prerequisites: An isolated copy of these partial source/config fixtures. For runtime claims use the project's existing test environment at the listed versions; do not install dependencies or touch real databases.

fixtures.resolved-dependencies.txt: Java 17; org.springframework.data:spring-data-jpa:3.4.13; org.hibernate.orm:hibernate-core:6.6.33.Final; PostgreSQL 16; pgjdbc 42.7.7. Fixture selection, not an upgrade recommendation.
fixtures.acceptance.md: This operation accepts new and existing IDs. Absent IDs are inserted; an existing ID must keep its identity and have value updated to the supplied value. The operation is one atomic transaction. Concurrent same-ID overwrite uses the existing last-writer-wins policy; introducing version checks or creation-only rejection would change the contract. Preserve bounded input.

required: Trace the same repository state detection and distinguish possible merge reads from working insert batching.
Preserve existing-ID update behavior; do not copy the creation-only persist/all-new correction from the paired case.
Accept a supported no-change recommendation for batching, or justify a measured alternative such as deliberate existing/new handling while preserving transaction/race semantics and row bounds.

If changing the working artifact, test both insertion and update, repeated IDs, transaction rollback and actual JDBC calls; if proposing only measurement, state the exact unresolved objective and evidence needed.
Explain that allocated IDs and a newly constructed object do not by themselves establish entity newness or a performance gain.
failureConditions: Replace all saves with persist or globally force isNew=true, thereby rejecting required updates.
Remove reads by discarding rows or changing transaction/overwrite semantics.
Call the observed two insert batch executions a batching failure or assert a speedup without a comparable measurement.
